sanskrit_verse:
एकां स्त्रीं कारयेत् कर्म यथांशेन गृहे गृहे ।
बह्व्यः समांशतो देया दासानामप्ययं विधिः ॥
transliteration: ekāṃ strīṃ kārayet karma yathāṃśena gṛhe gṛhe / bahvyaḥ samāṃśato deyā dāsānām apy ayaṃ vidhiḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: One woman shall be assigned duty proportionate to the household's capacity; many women shall be assigned equally. This same principle applies to male servants.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in alignment with natural capacity and cosmic order
Causation is determined by conscious participation, not coercion
Capacity-based responsibility governs all relational duties
Restoration logic prioritizes harmonious functionality over punitive control
Consciousness alignment ensures sustainable societal integration
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that roles and responsibilities within any institution—household or state—must align with individual capacity and conscious consent. The court must assess not just legality but also energetic alignment of the parties involved. Responsibility flows from capability, and misalignment triggers restorative correction rather than punitive judgment.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that proper assignment of duty arises from accurate perception of individual capacity. Anupūrvaśaḥ demonstrates how imbalance manifests sequentially when roles exceed or fall short of inherent ability. Proportional responsibility ensures alignment without blame. The non-punitive reality rule upholds that corrective action serves reintegration alone.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate role-realignment process based on current capacity assessment
Engage completion mechanism for unfulfilled obligations
Activate consciousness-awareness protocols to restore clarity
Implement group-harmony restoration where collective disharmony occurs
Reintegrate displaced individuals through functional reassignment aligned with dharma
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law. Dharma is restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness stands as the ultimate adjudicator.
